Answer: B
Reason: The initial chest X-ray shows dense consolidation in the right upper lobe with a bulging minor fissure, characteristic of Klebsiella pneumonia. The follow-up image demonstrates progression to cavitation and necrotizing changes within the consolidated area, which is a known complication of this infection, eventually leading to residual fibrosis as seen in the later image.
